requirements.businessContext: Per-team in-app notification feed. Lifecycle events from other modules (trade proposals, admin trade actions, gameweek scoring, release refunds, slot economy, club purchases) write rows into the `notifications` table via the shared `createNotification` helper. Signed-in team users see an unread badge in the global `NotificationBell`, a 3-item dropdown preview, and a paginated full feed at `/notifications`. The module owns CRUD (list, mark-read) only; emission of rows belongs to the source module, and email/push delivery is out of scope.

businessRules.rule: `notifications` table columns: id (PK text), teamId (FK teams.id, cascade delete), leagueId (FK leagues.id, cascade delete), type (text), title (text), body (text), link (nullable text), readAt (nullable timestamp), createdAt (timestamp, defaults to now()).
Composite index `notifications_team_unread` on (teamId, readAt) backs the unread-count and team-feed queries.

`NotificationType` is a closed string union: trade_proposed, trade_accepted, trade_rejected, trade_approved, trade_admin_rejected, trade_cancelled, gw_processed, release_refund, slot_redeemed, slot_unlocked, club_purchased. `createNotification` is the only sanctioned write path (plus the admin restore-auction importer).

GET /api/notifications requires a session cookie. Unauthenticated callers receive HTTP 401 'Not authenticated' (matching PATCH). Non-team sessions (admin/superadmin) receive HTTP 403 'Team access required'. Only team sessions reach the list-fetch path.
GET filters rows to the calling team only (`notifications.teamId = session.id`). An optional `?leagueId=` further restricts to a single league.
GET supports `page` (default 1) and `pageSize` (default 30, capped at 100, floor 1). Invalid/NaN inputs fall back to the defaults; `page` is clamped to `[1, totalPages]` when totalPages > 0.
Legacy `?limit=N` overrides `pageSize`, clamps to 1–100, and forces `page=1`. Provided for backward compatibility with older callers.
GET response always orders results by `createdAt DESC` (newest first).
GET response shape: `{ notifications: NotificationItem[], unreadCount, totalCount, page, pageSize, totalPages }`. `readAt` and `createdAt` are serialised as ISO strings (or null for `readAt`).
`unreadCount` reflects unread rows across ALL pages for the team (or league-scoped subset if `leagueId` is supplied), not just the current page.

Both GET and PATCH on /api/notifications return uniform auth responses: 401 with body.error='Not authenticated' for no session, 403 with body.error='Team access required' for non-team sessions. This makes the /notifications page client's status===401 redirect-to-signin branch reachable for anonymous visitors.
PATCH body must contain either `{ all: true }` or a non-empty `ids: string[]`. Any other shape (missing both, `ids:[]`, `all:false`) returns `400 { error: "Provide ids[] or all:true" }`.
PATCH `{ all: true }` sets `readAt = now()` for every UNREAD row owned by the calling team (already-read rows are not re-stamped).
PATCH `{ ids: [...] }` sets `readAt = now()` only on rows whose `teamId = session.id` AND `id ∈ ids`. IDs belonging to another team are silently ignored — no row leakage, no error.

There is no DELETE endpoint for individual notifications. Bulk deletion only occurs as a side-effect of `POST /api/admin/[leagueId]/restore-auction`, which wipes all notifications for the league before re-importing from the backup payload.
NotificationBell polls `/api/notifications` every 30 seconds while mounted and stores the latest snapshot (full default page + unreadCount) in component state.
Bell badge shows the numeric `unreadCount` for 1–9 and the literal string `9+` for any count ≥ 10. Badge is hidden when unread = 0.
Bell dropdown shows at most the first 3 items from the loaded list; a See all link navigates to `/notifications`.
Clicking a notification (in bell or feed) marks it read server-side first. The client only updates local state on a 2xx response, so a 5xx leaves the badge consistent with persisted state.
Clicking a notification with a non-null `link` navigates to that link AFTER attempting the mark-read. Already-read notifications skip the PATCH and navigate immediately.
`/notifications` page uses pageSize=50 (UI constant). The bell uses the server default of 30. Both fall within the 100 cap.

TRIGGER trade_proposed: POST /api/auction/trade fires one notification to the target team after the proposal row is inserted, body="{proposerDisplay} sent you a trade proposal", link=`/{slug}/marketplace?tab=incoming`. `proposerDisplay` prefers the proposer's PL Club Auction club name if owned, else the team name, else literal "A team".

TRIGGER trade_rejected: PATCH /api/auction/trade with action=reject fires one notification to the proposer, body="{targetDisplay} rejected your trade proposal", link=`/{slug}/marketplace?tab=outgoing` (link omitted if league row not found).

TRIGGER trade_accepted: PATCH /api/auction/trade with action=accept fires one notification to the proposer after re-validation passes, body="{targetDisplay} accepted your trade — awaiting admin approval", link=`/{slug}/marketplace?tab=outgoing`.

TRIGGER trade_approved: POST /api/auction/trade/admin action=approve fires one notification to BOTH proposer and target after `executeTrade` succeeds. Title="Trade approved", body="Admin approved the trade — players & cash have been transferred", link tab=history.

TRIGGER trade_admin_rejected: POST /api/auction/trade/admin action=reject fires one notification to BOTH parties. Title="Trade rejected by admin", body="Admin rejected the trade", link tab=history. Only allowed when proposal.status ∈ {pending, accepted}.

TRIGGER trade_cancelled: POST /api/auction/trade/admin action=cancel fires one notification to BOTH parties. Title="Trade cancelled", body="Admin cancelled the trade", link tab=history. Refused if proposal.status = completed.

TRIGGER gw_processed: `processAuctionGameweek` fires one notification per ranked team after a successful scoring transaction. Body includes rank, points, and payout in £M. Link=`/{slug}/gw-results?gw={gwNumber}`. Skipped on the race-loss path (another caller already scored).

TRIGGER release_refund: `processAuctionGameweek` fires one notification per team that received a refund this GW, body="£{X}M for {N} released player(s)", link=`/{slug}/finance`. Singular vs plural is grammatical on count===1.

TRIGGER slot_redeemed: POST /api/auction/redeem-slot fires one best-effort notification to the redeeming team, body="£{X}M deducted · {N} slot(s) remaining", link=`/{slug}/auction`. Failure to notify is logged but never fails the redemption response.

TRIGGER slot_unlocked: POST /api/auction/unlock-slot fires one best-effort notification to the unlocking team, title="Unlocked slot {N}", body shows £ deducted and new squad cap. No link. Failure logged, not surfaced.

TRIGGER club_purchased: `settleClubAuction` fires one best-effort notification to the winning bidder when a club is sold, title="You bought {playerName}", body details purchase price, tier, and rename behaviour. Failures are logged but do not roll back the auction settlement.

All trigger sites (trade approval/rejection/cancellation aside) wrap `createNotification` in try/catch and only log on failure — notification failure must never roll back the underlying business action (scoring, slot purchase, club purchase).

`createNotification` assigns the row id via `generateId()` and persists `link = input.link ?? null`. `readAt` is left null on insert (unread by default). `createdAt` defaults to `new Date()` from the schema.
Deleting a team or league cascades to its notifications (`onDelete: "cascade"` on both FKs).

defects.title: GET /api/notifications returns 200 empty payload instead of 401 for unauthenticated callers
defects.description: src/app/api/notifications/route.ts:20-26 short-circuits with a 200 JSON response (`notifications:[], unreadCount:0, ...`) whenever there is no session OR the session is not type='team'. The /notifications page client at src/app/notifications/page.tsx:34-41 explicitly checks `res.status === 401` to redirect to /signin — that branch is therefore unreachable.
defects.expectedBehaviour: GET should return 401 for unauthenticated callers (mirroring PATCH behaviour) so the client can route them to /signin. Admin/superadmin sessions can keep returning empty (legitimately no notifications) or also 401 — but the two endpoints should agree.
defects.actualBehaviour: An unauthenticated visitor at /notifications sees a permanent "You're all caught up" empty state and is never redirected to sign in. Inconsistent with PATCH which returns 401.
defects.notes: Two fixes possible: (a) tighten GET to return 401 when !session — matches PATCH and lets page.tsx redirect work; (b) keep current behaviour and remove the dead 401 branch from page.tsx (less safe — silently swallows logged-out state). Option (a) is preferred. Low-risk change; only affects callers without a team session. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean for the touched file. [QA-VERIFIED] Inverted pinning TC(s). [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: GET /api/notifications now returns HTTP 401 'Not authenticated' when there is no session, and HTTP 403 'Team access required' when the session is not type='team' (src/app/api/notifications/route.ts:20-32). Previously returned 200 with an empty payload, leaving the /notifications page client in a confusing logged-out-but-rendered state. The page's `status===401` redirect-to-signin branch is now reachable.
